explanation:
[EFFECT] The day of the week has a non-monotonic effect on predicted hourly demand. Sunday (weekday = 0) consistently produces the most negative average contribution, meaning the model predicts lower demand on Sundays, all else equal. Mid-week days (Monday through Thursday, values 1–4) show a modest but reliably positive contribution, nudging demand upward. Saturday (value 6) and Sunday (value 0) both display very wide spreads of SHAP values — meaning their influence swings strongly positive or negative depending on the hour and other conditions — while weekdays show a tighter, more consistently positive effect.

[IMPORTANCE] Weekday is the **4th most important** feature in the model out of nine, with an importance score of 0.173. It is significantly less influential than the hour of day (0.833), but roughly on par with year (0.200) and temperature (0.197), making it a meaningful but secondary driver of demand.

[RECOMMENDATION] Since weekdays (especially Monday–Thursday) tend to boost predicted demand while Sundays reduce it, consider maintaining fuller bike availability and staffing levels on weekdays and adjusting resources downward on Sundays — while remaining flexible on Saturdays, where demand can swing widely depending on the time of day.
